That sounds like an incredibly tedious workflow—essentially a digital version of "cutting and pasting" by hand. While it gets the job done, you're spending way more time on the logistics of the notes than on the actual thinking or organizing.

Since you are looking for a way to streamline this "gather and digitize" phase, here are a few ways to automate the cropping and typing steps.

1. The "Gold Standard" Solution: The Post-it® App

Even if you aren't using official Post-it brand notes, the Post-it® App (available on iOS and Android) is designed exactly for your use case.

  • Auto-Detection: You point your camera at the whiteboard, and it uses computer vision to "recognize" every individual square or rectangular card.
  • Instant Cropping: It crops them all into individual digital "tiles" in one tap.
  • Organization: Once captured, you can drag and drop them into groups or boards within the app.
  • Export: You can export them directly to PDF, PowerPoint, or Excel.

2. Leveraging Built-in OCR (Skip the Typing)

Since you already use Google Photos, you might be able to skip the "typing down the notes" part entirely.

  • Google Lens: If you open one of your note card photos in Google Photos on your phone or desktop, click "Copy Text." Google’s OCR is quite powerful and can usually handle handwriting reasonably well, allowing you to paste the text directly into your notes.
  • Apple Live Text: If you use an iPhone or Mac, you can highlight handwriting directly in the photo and "Copy All" to move it into a document.

3. Dedicated Whiteboard Scanners

Apps like Microsoft Lens or Adobe Scan have a specific "Whiteboard" mode.

  • They automatically remove the glare from the board, sharpen the handwriting, and "de-skew" the image (straighten it if you took the photo at an angle).
  • While they don't always split multiple cards automatically like the Post-it app, they do produce a much cleaner image for OCR to read.

4. Smart Whiteboard Accessories

If you do this frequently, you might look into Rocketbook Beacons. These are four orange "markers" you stick to the corners of your whiteboard.

  • The companion app looks for those markers to instantly crop and "blast" the image to a specific destination (Google Drive, Slack, Email).
  • It has a feature called "OCR Transcription" that can send you a text file of what was written on the board alongside the image.
